caption:
Is the reward for good [anything] but good?

Surah Ar-Rahman (55:60). Swipe through for the Arabic, then English, Mandarin, Korean, Japanese and Malay.

Sources on the final slide.

#Quran #ArRahman #Ihsan #IslamicReminder #Deen

sourcing.primary_text: Qur'an 55:60, Surah Ar-Rahman: a short, complete, single-ayah rhetorical question stating that the reward for good conduct (ihsan) is good in return. Chosen as today's post after checking it against all 30 previously published posts for this channel - no prior post has used Surah Ar-Rahman, and the theme (reciprocal goodness) is distinct from previously covered themes (gratitude, patience, hardship-and-ease, justice, tawakkul, etc).
sourcing.arabic: Edition quran-uthmani, api.alquran.cloud/v1/ayah/55:60/editions/quran-uthmani,en.sahih,zh.jian,ko.korean,ja.japanese,ms.basmeih, live-fetched 2026-09-27, HTTP 200. Slide text extracted programmatically from the raw API response field (data[].text keyed by edition identifier) and asserted byte-identical to the on-disk slide JSON before this record was written. No formatting artifacts present in the source string.
sourcing.english: Edition en.sahih (Saheeh International), same live API call, HTTP 200. Extracted programmatically and asserted byte-identical to source. No formatting artifacts.
sourcing.chinese: Edition zh.jian (Ma Jian translation), same live API call, HTTP 200. Extracted programmatically and asserted byte-identical to source. No formatting artifacts.
sourcing.korean: Edition ko.korean, same live API call, HTTP 200. Edition metadata lists englishName 'Unknown' for the translator, so the citation slide reads 'translator not specified by source'. Extracted programmatically and asserted byte-identical to source. No formatting artifacts found (no stray split-word spaces of the kind seen on other posts using this edition).
sourcing.japanese: Edition ja.japanese, same live API call, HTTP 200. Same 'Unknown' translator metadata as Korean, so the citation slide also reads 'translator not specified by source' for Japanese. Extracted programmatically and asserted byte-identical to source.
sourcing.malay: Edition ms.basmeih (Abdullah Muhammad Basmeih), same live API call, HTTP 200. Extracted programmatically and asserted byte-identical to source. No formatting artifacts.
sourcing.verification_note: All six editions live-fetched in a single API call this session (2026-09-27) from api.alquran.cloud, HTTP 200. Every slide's text was written directly from the raw API response fields programmatically (never hand-typed) and re-read from disk and asserted byte-for-byte equal to the corresponding API response field before this meta.json was written. An initial hand-typed draft of the Arabic slide text was attempted first, failed a byte-identity assertion against the API response (a Unicode normalisation mismatch invisible to the eye), and was discarded in favour of the programmatic extraction used in the final files - the same category of error documented on quran-14-7. Caption pull-quote (the English text) asserted equal to the corrected/verified English slide text. No wording generated from memory.
sourcing.compliance_check: Checked programmatically this session against every string term in scripts/data/compliance-policy.json's halal section (prohibited, superstition, origins_patterns) across all slide text, title, caption and tags, using word-boundary regex matching. No hits. Pure typography, no imagery, so animate_imagery and context_review do not apply. House style: no em or en dashes, no emoji, UK spelling used throughout the caption.
